task_instance: Build a minimal MCP server (TypeScript, Streamable HTTP transport) that exposes a `render_profile` tool returning structuredContent, backed by a React + Fluent UI 'Profile Card' widget served as a compiled bundle through an MCP `ui://widget/profile-card.html` resource (text/html+skybridge), and verify it end-to-end with the MCP Inspector CLI as the skill's mandated workflow prescribes (tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/read, plus /health and /widgets/*.html and /assets/*.js HTTP checks).
evidence: Project at mcp-server/ with src/index.ts (Streamable HTTP /mcp endpoint, CORS for m365.cloud.microsoft, /health, /widgets/*.html, /assets static route), widgets/src/profile-card/{ProfileCard.tsx,main.tsx} (React + FluentProvider + Fluent tokens/components, useOpenAiGlobal('toolOutput') pattern with 'Unknown' fallback and email button hidden on Unknown per best-practices.md), widgets/profile-card.html (shell loader referencing built JS), vite.widget.config.ts. `npm install` succeeded (304 packages). `npx vite build -c vite.widget.config.ts` produced assets/profile-card.js (343.74 kB, gzip 100.24 kB) confirming the React+Fluent UI bundle actually compiles. Server started in background via `nohup npx tsx src/index.ts &` (per skill's BACKGROUND PROCESSES rule) and verified live: curl /health -> {"status":"ok"}; curl /widgets/profile-card.html -> shell HTML with resolved serverUrl; curl -I /assets/profile-card.js -> HTTP 200. MCP Inspector CLI (v0.20.0, exact command from skill) against http://localhost:3001/mcp: tools/list returned render_profile with full inputSchema and _meta.openai/outputTemplate; tools/call render_profile with name/title/email args returned structuredContent {name,title,email} plus _meta.openai/widgetAccessible:true and _meta.openai/outputTemplate, matching the skill's required tool response format exactly; resources/list returned the ui://widget/profile-card.html resource with mimeType text/html+skybridge; resources/read returned the widget shell HTML plus _meta with openai/widgetDomain and openai/widgetCSP. Server subsequently stopped with pkill. Not attempted/out of scope for this minimal instance (deliberately deferred, not required to prove the skill's core capability): devtunnel exposure (devtunnel CLI is not installed/available in this sandbox and would need an account/auth), mcpPlugin.json + M365 Copilot manifest provisioning via `atk provision` (requires an M365/Azure account and login), and live rendering inside the actual M365 Copilot Chat UI (an external hosted service requiring an account). These are downstream deployment/integration steps beyond the skill's core deliverable of 'an MCP server that implements the Copilot widget protocol and serves a React+Fluent UI widget,' which was built and verified working.
